frontier.hypothesis: func_80052B7C = gte_SetRotMatrix(a0) + gte_ldv0(a2) + gte_rt() + gte_stlvl(a3), plus one small written __asm__ island for the macro-less TR-from-halfwords chunk (citing the existing inline_asm_canonical.txt:340 grant), lands at sandbox distance 0.
frontier.mechanism: pure instruction-identity reproduction of an already owner-authorized whole-function asm leaf; no GCC-internals lever needed -- the only risk is whether GCC's volatile-asm statement ordering across the 5 chunks reproduces the original's exact instruction sequence.
frontier.next_probe: Apply memory/grind/func_80052B7C/candidate.c to src/main/3AB48.c (add #include <psxsdk/inline_o.h>, remove the INCLUDE_ASM line), run sandbox func_80052B7C --disable all --diff; if nonzero, read tmp/grind/func_80052B7C/dumps/.sched via dump.ps1 to see which chunk's scheduling diverges.

frontier.hypothesis: If the macro-call draft does not reach 0, the divergence is instruction ORDER between chunks 1-2 (target batches all 5+3 loads before any ctc2; a naive macro-call sequence may interleave load/ctc2 differently per-macro).
frontier.mechanism: GCC schedules across separate volatile __asm__ statements more freely than within one; cop2 latency nops may end up in different relative positions.
frontier.next_probe: Compare the macro-call build's .s against asm/funcs/func_80052B7C.s chunk-by-chunk; if order differs, consider whether the macros themselves (not a restructuring of C) already force the right order, or whether this is evidence the chunk needs to stay a single written island like chunk 2.

frontier.hypothesis: Chunk 2 (TR load from 3 sign-extended halfwords) requires an owner ruling-request: is a written __asm__ island for a macro-less GTE op still admissible under the existing per-function inline_asm_canonical.txt:340 grant, given the 2026-10-15 policy's general preference for macro calls?
frontier.mechanism: policy-interpretation question, not a codegen question -- only ask if frontier items 1-2 leave chunk 2 as the sole remaining blocker.
frontier.next_probe: Only after measuring (1); if everything else lands clean and chunk 2's written form is the only sticking point, file a precise ruling-request rather than guessing.
